summary: MARSCOPE is an interactive 3D Mars exploration and planning platform developed to help future explorers understand Martian terrain and plan safer surface journeys. It combines NASA’s Viking global imagery with Mars Global Surveyor’s MOLA elevation data and shaded-relief imagery to provide a layered view of the Martian surface. Users can explore locations, inspect elevation and terrain slope, view rover and lander sites, and generate terrain-aware routes using an experimental A* pathfinding algorithm. The platform also includes preliminary landing-site suitability assessment and comparison based on terrain slope and elevation. MARSCOPE addresses the challenge by bringing Mars surface data and exploration-planning tools together in one interactive interface, supporting better-informed decisions for future Marswalks and surface missions.
details:
Project Details – MARSCOPE

MARSCOPE is an interactive 3D Mars exploration platform designed to support future surface exploration and Marswalk planning.

How It Works

MARSCOPE displays Mars as an interactive 3D globe with multiple scientific map layers, including NASA's Viking global imagery and Mars Global Surveyor's MOLA shaded-relief imagery. It also uses MOLA elevation data to calculate surface elevation and terrain slope at selected locations.

Users can explore important rover and lander sites, inspect terrain information, and plan routes between selected locations. An experimental A* pathfinding algorithm searches for routes that account for terrain slope, estimates travel distance and time, and displays terrain-risk categories. The Landing Intelligence feature provides preliminary landing-site suitability scores based on elevation and slope, allowing users to compare candidate locations.

Benefits and Intended Impact

MARSCOPE brings different types of Martian surface information and exploration tools into one interactive interface. It helps users understand terrain conditions, identify challenging areas, compare potential landing locations, and explore possible routes. Its goal is to support better-informed planning for future robotic and human exploration of Mars.

Technology Used

  • Frontend: React.js and JavaScript
  • 3D Visualization: CesiumJS
  • Mapping: NASA planetary map tile services
  • Scientific Data: MOLA elevation dataset and Viking global imagery
  • Development Tools: Visual Studio Code, Node.js, Vite and Git
  • Hosting: Vercel

Creativity and Design Considerations

The main creative aspect of MARSCOPE is combining 3D planetary visualization, scientific terrain analysis, route planning and landing-site comparison in a single application. During development, we considered terrain slope, elevation, route distance, missing elevation data, usability and the need to present complex scientific information in an understandable way.

MARSCOPE is an experimental planning and visualization tool. Its route and landing assessments are preliminary and are not certified for actual astronaut navigation or spacecraft landing.
